While the case may be made against certain GMOs (Looking at you, Roundup Ready seeds), to insist on a ban on all future GMOs until they prove they are safe is not just a display on the ignorance of science, especially in what we have been doing with crops and livestock for literally thousands of years...but to show an ignorance of how government in general is supposed to work. Let's start with the most obvious issue: Burden of proof.

If Stein wants to place a moratorium (a de facto ban) on new GMOs, then it is incumbent upon her to prove they are unsafe to justify the ban. Trying to work a ban from the other way around does a runaround around the compelling interest and strict scrutiny tests required by the Supreme Court. Using the same logic, I could say that because some toys have resulted in the injuries of children, before any more toys are produced, they must prove they are completely safe. And yet there are problems with this argument, as well.

A) If you cannot produce a new toy until you have proven it is safe, you have effectively made sure that no new toys can be produced, because you cannot run tests to test whether a specific toy is safe until you physically produce that toy to run it through the gamut of tests. By testing the toy, you have already violated the law, because you produced something that was banned before it was clear for production. That you produced it for the sole purpose of testing, is irrelevant. Thus, a ban on production of new products "Until they are cleared by the government for safety" amounts to a de facto complete ban disguising itself as a partial ban to make it more palatable.

B) American government does not start from a position of "You can only do what we say you can do." That position is inherently authoritarian, which funnels back into your statement that authoritarian leftists are the problem. If the government wants to ban GMOs, then they must make, on a case-by-case basis, the case for banning these products. In certain cases (Roundup Ready) I would agree, and even support the case that certain GMOs are dangerous enough to the environment and public health to require banning. But you cannot enact a blanket ban on all GMOs without massively overreaching either Executive or Congressional authority.

C) We've been manipulating the genetics of crops and livestock for thousands of years. The modern dairy and beef cows would not exist today, had we not specifically bred them to those standards for the genetic traits we desired in them. In a time when California is experiencing record drought aggravated by farming in the region, and at a time when the Susquehanna river is primarily polluted by manure runoff, figuring out how to produce GMOs that require less water and nitrogen to produce similar yields would be godsends to these areas! With a "blanket moratorium", however, nobody is going to invest in the research necessary to produce these innovations. GMO's have already massively cut down on the amount of fossil fuels burned, land used (which reduces deforestation), and in many cases Pesticide usage (Roundup Ready, of course, being exempt from this classification). Aren't these the stated goals of environmental reformists everywhere in regards to the farming industry? Reduce fossil fuel consumption, reduce deforestation, and stop/slow the rate at which we're pumping chemicals into the ground and our plant life? Once those are addressed, the only really big thing left is inhumane factory-farming practices. A blanket moratorium, instead of a case-by-case ban on certain GMOs, is both anti-science and throws the baby out with the bathwater.

The argument regarding the safety and efficiency of GMOs is over. By and large, they are some of the safest things in the world, with very few exclusions that rise to the level of justifying banning or regulating them. Even the environmentalist that founded the Anti-GMO movement has admitted that he was wrong, and that his reasoning was based in emotive reasoning, and not in scientific reasoning. To quote Mr. Lynas on the matter: "You are more likely to get hit by an asteroid than you are to get hurt by GMO food."
